messages.subject_clean: Color specific tips containing certain letters/words
messages.body_plain:
Hello, is there a way to use grepl for multiple different strings? That is, to color all tips containing "ABC" one color and "DEF" another color? Further, is it possible to specify the color(s)?

Thank you!

messages.subject: Coloring single tip node based on label
messages.subject_clean: Coloring single tip node based on label
messages.body_plain:
I don't actually need anything, but I thought I'd leave this here for the next person.

I wanted to adjust the color of a single node on my tree based on its label. I didn't need anything fancy, so my google search wasn't helpful.

The following changes the node of "interesting_sample" red.

```
tree <- read.newick("iqtree.treefile")

ggtree(tree)  + geom_tippoint(aes(subset=(label==interesting_sample)), color = "red")
```

messages.body_plain:
Thank you for the reply. I'm not sure how I missed that in the manual. However, I was not able to make ggtext work for my circular tree where the labels need to be rotated. I'm sure I'm missing something.

However, I did find an answer to my original question and it is very simple, based on Guangchuang's answer above and the topic that was just posted about labeling specific tip points.

geom_tiplab2(aes(subset=grepl("Aa", label)), color="#999999") #All tip labels with "Aa" in them will be colored #999999 and the label is kept as text.

Thank you all!

messages.subject_clean: Color specific tips containing certain letters/words
messages.body_plain:
I thought you would like to color the tips in a way like this: Aa(in red)_Bb(in blue).

If you want to color tips in the way - if tips contain Aa, color in red, and color tips that contain Bb in blue, I think a better solution is to derive a variable (e.g., type) that contains Aa and Bb based on the tip labels. Then you can use geom_tiplab(aes(color = type)) to color the tips.

messages.subject: Re: Display Categorised Bootstrap Values.
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Happy New Year!

Please find attached the relevant files that are necessary for the complete reproduction of my code above. I would greatly appreciate any help.
The phylogeny was created using RAxML-NG.

Best regards, George.

On Saturday, 18 December 2021 at 17:20:06 UTC+1 guangc...@gmail.com wrote:
> see example in G Yu*. Using ggtree to Visualize Data on Tree-Like Structure <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpbi.96>. Current Protocols in Bioinformatics. 2020, 69(1):e96.
>
> If you want someone to help, you need to learn how to provide a reproducible example.
>
>
> On Wed, Dec 15, 2021 at 11:10 PM George Pacheco <rame...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Dear all,
> >
> > I would like to know if it would be possible to organically display categorised bootstrap values rather than a single value. Please consider my code below.
> >
> > Many thanks in advance, George.
> >
> > # Reads datasets ~
> > Data <- read.tree(file = "FPG--GoodSamples_NoSrisoriaNoCpalumbus_100BSs.raxml.support")
> >
> > # Reads annotations ~
> > Data_annot <- read.table("FPG--GoodSamples_FPG--GoodSamples_NoSrisoriaNoCpalumbus.annot", sep = "\t", header = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
> > colnames(Data_annot) <- c("label", "Population")
> >
> > # Expands the data by adding BioStatus ~
> > Data_annot$BioStatus <- ifelse(Data_annot$Population %in% c("Torshavn","Ejde","Sumba","LjosAir","Kunoy","Nolsoy", "Crete", "Sardinia","Vernelle","WadiHidan","PigeonIsland","Trincomalee"), "Remote_Localities_Within_Natural_Range",
> >                         ifelse(Data_annot$Population %in% c("Guimaraes","Lisbon","Barcelona","Berlin","Cambridge",
> >                                                             "Colombo","Copenhagen","London","Prague","Jihlava","Abadeh",
> >                                                             "Isfahan","Lahijan","Nowshahr","Tehran","TelAviv"), "Urban_Localities_Within_Natural_Range",
> >                         ifelse(Data_annot$Population %in% c("SaltLakeCity","Denver", "FeralVA", "FeralUT", "TlaxcalaDeXicohtencatl",
> >                                                             "MexicoCity","Monterrey","SanCristobalDeLasCasas","Santiago",
> >                                                             "Salvador","Tatui","Johannesburg","Nairobi","Perth"), "Localities_Outside_Natural_Range",
> >                         ifelse(Data_annot$Population %in% c("TelAvivColony","Wattala", "Wellawatte"), "Captives", NA))))
> >
> > # Melts the annotation dataset ~
> > Data_annot <- melt(Data_annot)
